name: Darcey Edwards

bio.statement: Her official page says she represents residents of Columbia County and parts of Multnomah, Washington and Yamhill counties.
bio.excerpt: It’s an honor to serve and represent the people of Columbia County and parts of Multnomah, Washington, and Yamhill Counties

source.publisher: Oregon Legislature

bio.statement: Ballotpedia says her career experience includes owning a real estate agency.
bio.excerpt: Darcey Edwards' career experience includes owning a real estate agency.

source.publisher: Ballotpedia

bio.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Edwards lists her occupation as state representative, small business owner and principal broker, with a background in housing, economic development and chamber of commerce work.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: State Representative; Small business owner; Principal Broker, Edwards Realty Trust Occupational Background: Housing, Economic development, Chamber of Commerce

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

bio.statement: Edwards lists Banks High School as her education and state representative as her prior governmental experience.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: Banks High School Prior Governmental Experience: State Representative

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Edwards cites helping pass legislation to protect students and law enforcement from false emergency reports.
positions.excerpt: helped pass legislation that will protect students and law enforcement from dangerous false emergency reports

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Edwards cites helping pass a ban on AI tools from hostile foreign companies on state systems.
positions.excerpt: ban AI tools from hostile foreign companies on state systems

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Edwards cites helping cut red tape so families can rebuild homes lost to disasters more quickly.
positions.excerpt: cut unnecessary red tape so families can rebuild homes lost to disasters more quickly

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Edwards cites passing a law helping family forestland owners keep land across generations, and says she will defend farming, timber, hunting and fishing.
positions.excerpt: I also passed a law helping family forestland owners keep their land across generations instead of being forced to sell to pay estate taxes

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Edwards cites helping secure funding for local services including the Banks Fire District and the Amani Center.
positions.excerpt: Delivering Where It Counts. I helped secure funding for important local services like the Banks Fire District

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

voting_record.statement: Her March 2026 session summary lists HB 4151, which it says holds individuals accountable for using emergency services to harass political opponents.
voting_record.excerpt: Holds individuals accountable for using emergency services to harass political opponents.

source.publisher: Oregon Legislature

voting_record.statement: Her March 2026 session summary lists SB 1561, a disaster-rebuilding bill allowing homeowners to restore or replace homes through a streamlined process.
voting_record.excerpt: Allows homeowners to restore or replace homes lost to disaster through a streamlined administrative process.

source.publisher: Oregon Legislature

voting_record.statement: Her March 2026 session summary lists SB 1573, which it says prohibits syringe service programs from mobile or temporary locations within 2,000 feet of schools and childcare.
voting_record.excerpt: Prohibits syringe service programs from operating mobile or temporary locations within 2,000 feet.

source.publisher: Oregon Legislature
